proof.criterion: A SIGKILLed drain loses no kept copy: after the 60 s claim window a later claim takes the abandoned claim over and every copy reaches a holder exactly once.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-listener processes built from this head on one real NATS server, each with a real session process; twelve copies kept for an unheld role, listener A claims, A is SIGKILLed the moment its claim returns, with its drain still running.
proof.observed: A was killed having logged 6 forwards, so it died with a copy claimed and unforwarded. A claim on listener B one second later delivered 0 of 12 — the claim was younger than roleKeepClaimWindow and B left the lane to it, which is the design. After waiting the 60 s window out, two further claims on B delivered the rest: exactly once 12 of 12, never 0, more than once 0. No loss and no duplicate across a hard kill.

findings.why it matters: skill://legion-worker has the reviewer fix prose-only findings itself and send code or behaviour back to the implementer. A reviewer that authored this fix would be approving its own code, so the approval that follows is not independent, and the merge gate's review round would not mean what it says. The code itself is correct and proven above — this is about who may author it and who may then approve it, which is the architect's to settle before the next review round.
